u.Después de dieciséis años, Hungría no es: After sixteen years, Hungary is not a formality. It is a duel.
u.Por primera vez desde que Orbán regresar: For the first time since Orbán returned to power in 2010, the result is not decided in advance. Not because the system has suddenly become fair, but because something harder to manipulate than electoral law has shifted: the patience of an electorate that grew weary but remained inert.
u.«No habrá nunca una puerta. Estás adentr: «There will never be a door. You are inside / and the fortress encompasses the universe / and has neither obverse nor reverse / nor outer wall nor secret centre.»
u.— Jorge Luis Borges, Elogio de la sombra: — Jorge Luis Borges, In Praise of Darkness, 1969
u.Hay una imagen que define la campaña que: There is one image that defines the campaign Hungary is living through these days. In the markets of central Budapest, beside the official government posters — where Péter Magyar is pictured alongside European flags and Brussels leaders, under the slogan «Don't let them destroy Hungary!» — TISZA activists have begun sticking their own stickers on top. Not with elaborate messages. Just with a date: 12 April. It is enough. After sixteen years of almost uncontested hegemony, the simple reminder that there is an election is, in itself, a subversive act.
u.Las elecciones parlamentarias del 12 de: The parliamentary elections of 12 April 2026 reach Hungary at a moment that nobody — neither Viktor Orbán's supporters nor his adversaries — had entirely anticipated. For the first time since Orbán returned to power in 2010, the result is not decided in advance. Not because the system has suddenly become fair — it has not — but because something harder to manipulate than electoral law has shifted: the patience of an electorate that grew weary but remained inert, and that found, in the improbable figure of a former member of the regime itself, a reason to vote again. [CSIS, March 2026]
u.Ese hombre se llama Péter Magyar. Y lo p: That man is called Péter Magyar. And the first thing to understand about him is that he is neither what his detractors say — an agent of Brussels, a traitor from the liberal wing — nor the regenerated democrat his followers project. Magyar is something stranger and more useful for the moment: an avowed conservative, nationalist and Christian who knows the inside of the Fidesz system because he inhabited it for years, and who decided, in a moment of simultaneous personal and political rupture, to use it against itself.
u.Como muchas veces en la historia de Euro: As has often happened in the history of eastern Europe, regime change emerges from former members of the old regime's political elite.
u.El insurgente que conoce los códigos del: The insurgent who knows the bunker's codes
u.En marzo de 2024, Magyar convocó una man: In March 2024, Magyar called a demonstration in central Budapest. Tens of thousands responded. It was no prodigy of political organisation: it was the product of something more volatile and harder to sustain, which is moral rage. The scandals that had shaken the government weeks earlier — linked, precisely, to the child protection system Fidesz had erected as one of its ideological pillars — had exposed a hypocrisy that even the party's most loyal voters found hard to defend out loud.
u.Magyar no llegó con un programa detallad: Magyar did not arrive with a detailed programme. He arrived with something more valuable for that political moment: the credential of having been inside. He knew how the machine worked. He knew where the wires ran. And his central appeal — that the regime had betrayed its own founding principles, those of a sovereign, proud and clean Hungary — resonated with a segment of the electorate the cosmopolitan left had never been able to reach: moderate rural voters, middle-class families who had benefited from Fidesz's social policies but could no longer ignore the systemic corruption that financed them.
u.En las elecciones europeas de junio de 2: In the European elections of June 2024, TISZA obtained almost 30% of the vote — a result nobody had foreseen in that timeframe, for a party that had not existed three months earlier. Since then the question has not been whether Magyar is a phenomenon, but whether he is a durable one. And the answer, a few weeks from 12 April, remains genuinely uncertain.
u.Las encuestas húngaras se han convertido: Hungarian polls have become, in the months before the election, a battlefield in their own right. Institutes aligned with the government show Fidesz with leads of between 5 and 10 points. Independent institutes show TISZA with similar or larger leads. The political analyst Gábor Török observed in January 2026 that the differences between government-aligned and independent pollsters were a "new phenomenon" in Hungarian politics, "inexplicable on research grounds". [Wikipedia — Opinion polling for the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary election]
u.Medián, uno de los más reputados en el p: Medián, one of the most reputable in the country, published 40% for TISZA against 33% for Fidesz in January 2026. Závecz Research showed a 10-point opposition lead among certain voters. The aggregator PolitPro placed TISZA at 48.7% and Fidesz at 40.8% in early April. [PolitPro Poll Trend, April 2026] Bloomberg reported on 1 April that TISZA reached 56% among decided voters against 37% for Fidesz according to the institute 21 Kutatóközpont. [Bloomberg, 1 Apr. 2026] Institutes linked to the government or funded by friendly media, for their part, showed the inverse figures — Fidesz around 43% and TISZA at 37% — although their methodologies have been publicly questioned by Hungarian researchers.
u.Lo que esta guerra de cifras revela no e: What this war of figures reveals is not only the polarisation of the media ecosystem — already familiar — but something more fundamental: the political information system in Hungary is so captured that not even the actors themselves know precisely what is happening. Fidesz retains between 200,000 and 300,000 inactive voters who could be mobilised in the final stretch. TISZA's voters, by contrast, are already hyper-mobilised, with little room for growth from within their own ranks. The election will be decided, as usually happens in mixed representation systems, in a handful of single-member constituencies where the gerrymandering Fidesz practised in 2021 — a redistribution obliging the opposition to win by 3 to 5 points in the national vote in order to secure a majority — could prove decisive.
u.La economía que no cuadra: The economy that does not add up
u.Detrás de la retórica de la soberanía y: Behind the rhetoric of sovereignty and the campaign posters, Hungary's fiscal numbers tell a less heroic story. The public deficit is projected at 5.2% of GDP for 2026 — well above the limits of the European Stability Pact. Growth, which during the 2010s was Orbán's most solid argument before his own electorate, has moderated to 2.3% a year, weighed down by debt that does not fall below 74% of GDP and by the most persistent inflation in the region. To compensate, the government has deployed an arsenal of pro-cyclical measures in the months before the election: pension increases, lifetime income tax exemption for mothers with two or more children, soft loans for home buyers. These are policies that buy electoral loyalty at a cost any incoming government — of any stripe — will have to absorb.
u.El otro freno es Bruselas, y aquí el dañ: The other brake is Brussels, and here the damage is no longer merely potential. Hungary has definitively lost access to more than €1 billion in European funds by failing to implement the judicial and anti-corruption reforms the Commission required before the end of 2025. For a country whose infrastructure and development model have historically depended on Community transfers, this self-inflicted financial isolation is beginning to show in public services and in the daily cost of living. Into that vacuum, Chinese capital has presented itself as an alternative — major investments in batteries, logistics infrastructure, semiconductors — but at a cost that goes beyond the financial.
u.Bajo el mandato de Orbán, Hungría se con: Under Orbán's rule, Hungary became the principal recipient of Chinese direct investment in the European Union — a position that is neutral neither economically nor geopolitically. The relationship with Beijing has served Orbán as a bargaining lever against Brussels: an implicit reminder that he has options. But it has also installed him in a contradiction that his own allies on the global right are beginning to point out with discomfort: it is difficult to present oneself as the champion of Western sovereignty while allowing Chinese surveillance technology to penetrate the digital infrastructure of a NATO member.
u.Esta tensión tiene consecuencias concret: This tension has concrete consequences for cybersecurity. Western intelligence services — particularly those of Germany, Poland and the Baltic states — have warned for years about Hungary's ambivalent position between the Alliance's information systems and the interests of Beijing, and of Moscow too. Budapest has access to classified NATO intelligence while simultaneously hosting digital infrastructure linked to Chinese companies subject to the People's Republic's national security law. That dual belonging is a vector of vulnerability that the April election will not resolve in either direction: an Orbán victory will deepen it; a Magyar victory will make it explicit and force painful decisions about signed contracts and established relationships.
u.Lo que distingue esta campaña de las ant: What distinguishes this campaign from earlier ones is not only its competitiveness but its technology. The use of deepfakes and AI-generated video to distort Magyar's statements is already a documented practice. The government has systematically amplified conspiracy theories about foreign funding for TISZA — some based on real judicial proceedings in Belgium and Spain, others outright fabrications — through the media it controls, which represent the most sophisticated network of media capture any government has built inside the European Union. Orbán does not merely dominate the channels: he has redesigned the information ecosystem so that fact-checking is structurally more costly than the diffusion of falsehoods.
u.Para la oposición, el desafío no es solo: For the opposition, the challenge is not only to win votes — it is to break a bubble. In the 2022 elections, a six-party coalition with more resources and better organisation than any previous opposition lost by 20 points to Fidesz. The lesson Magyar draws from that defeat is that fragmentation and the lack of a coherent narrative are more lethal than media control. TISZA has built a more disciplined campaign with a simpler message. Whether it is enough, 12 April will tell.
u.Un mensaje de campaña que mantiene la op: It is a campaign message that maintains opposition to the war in Ukraine and does not speak of flexibility on so-called woke agenda issues. It focuses on growing the economy, bringing down inflation, easing the rising cost of living and cleaning Orbánist corruption out of politics so as to unlock the blocked EU funds.
u.Los dos escenarios y lo que no está en j: The two scenarios and what is not at stake
u.Los analistas que estudian el sistema in: Analysts who study the Hungarian institutional system point to a fact the polls tend to obscure: winning the election and winning power are not the same thing. Fidesz spent its three two-thirds majorities — between 2010 and 2022 — building a legal and institutional architecture designed to survive an ordinary electoral defeat. The Constitutional Court judges are Fidesz appointees with mandates running to 2032 and 2034. The Central Bank and the Prosecutor General are politically captured offices. The Sovereignty Protection Office — created in 2023 with powers to investigate civil society organisations — was explicitly designed as an instrument for harassing the opposition in the event of a transition. A Magyar victory without a two-thirds majority — the most likely scenario if he wins — would mean governing with his hands tied by an institutional order built by his adversary.
u.Hay, además, una dimensión que las narra: There is, moreover, a dimension that regime-change narratives tend to underestimate: the economic cost of the transition itself. A massive review of the last decade's state contracts — which is what a TISZA government would have to do to dismantle Orbánist crony capitalism — would generate first-order regulatory uncertainty for investors, precisely at the moment the country needs financing to absorb the inherited deficit. The transition from a clientelist system to a competitive market one, within the short span of a single parliamentary term, is a process no post-communist democracy has completed without turbulence. Poland tried. The result remains to be seen.
u.Si Orbán gana, el impacto no se contendr: If Orbán wins, the impact will not be contained within Hungary's borders. For the international national-populist right — from the MAGA movements to the sovereigntist factions of western Europe — Budapest has served as a demonstration that the illiberal model is electorally and administratively viable over the long term. A Magyar defeat, achieved by mobilising rural voters along the «war or peace» axis — the narrative with which Orbán has framed his stance on Ukraine — would offer an updated manual on how populist leaders can turn foreign policy into a domestic lever. If Magyar wins, the demonstration would be the opposite: that illiberal systems have internal cracks their own actors can exploit, and it would probably affect the material conditions of many of those movements seeking power in various countries.
u.La noche del 12 de abril, cuando cierren: On the night of 12 April, when the polling stations close in Budapest and in the villages of the interior, Hungary will learn whether Orbán is the durable exception to the European liberal model or simply its longest parenthesis. The rest of the continent will watch with a mixture of intellectual interest and practical anxiety. Because what the Hungarian electorate decides affects not only Hungary: it affects the European Union's capacity to remain, in any operative sense, a political community with shared values, and not merely a market with a common currency and external borders.
u.En los mercados de Budapest, mientras ta: In the markets of Budapest, meanwhile, someone goes on sticking up stickers bearing a date. It is a small gesture. But in systems built to make the calendar irrelevant, reminding people that there is a day on which their vote counts may still be the most radical political act of all. We shall see whether, as in Borges's famous story, once inside no one can escape the labyrinth.
